name: Diagnostic_LOG_1
questiontext:
Imagine you have a deck of four cards in which you know every card has one letter on one side and one number on the other. You can see the following:

{{CT:0}}
{{CT:1}}
{{CT:2}}
{{CT:3}}

You must choose the fewest cards to turn over to establish the truth of the following statement.

"Every card which has a {{CT:4}} on one side has a {{CT:5}} on the other."

Which cards will you turn over? Your answer should be a set of cards, e.g. {?, ...}.

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Turning over all the cards is not the right answer. While it does enable you to establish whether this is true, it is not the fewest possible cards.

One way to think about this statement is to re-phrase it to

"If we see a {{CT:4}} on one side then we have a {{CT:5}} on the other."

Keep in mind that every card has a number on one side and a letter on the other!

Do we turn over the {{CT:4}}? Yes, if we see a {{CT:4}} then we must check if we have a {{CT:5}}. This kind of if-then statement is known as implication.

Do we turn over the {{CT:6}}? Yes, if we have a {{CT:4}} and a {{CT:6}} then the statement is false. Hence we must check for this possibility. We can re-phrase the statement to

"If we do not have a {{CT:5}} on one side then we do not have {{CT:4}} on the other."

This form is known as the contrapositive. It is equivalent to the original statement we are trying to check.

Do we turn over the {{CT:7}}? No, since we have not satisfied the hypothesis that we have one {{CT:4}}. The other side must be a number but we don't care if it is a {{CT:5}} or not. Any situation does not affect the truth of the statement we are trying to check.

Do we turn over the {{CT:5}}? No, since we could easily have {{CT:4}} on one side and a {{CT:5}} on the other. The statement is unaffected. Similarly if we don't have a {{CT:4}} on the other side the statement is unaffected.

prts.name: prt1

on_true.feedback: You certainly don't need to turn them all over! Please turn over the those, and only those, which will establish the truth of this statement.
